summary: Lozang Samten studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from circa 1978 to 1983 and held a post there around 1993.

Luca Maria Olivieri works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin (c. 2006–2010), he served as director of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and joined Ca' Foscari University of Venice c. 2020.

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She served at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015).
Lucia Galli works in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford, where she also held an academic post.

Indologist Lucian Scherman studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Ernst Kuhn at Munich, where he completed his Promotion and Habilitation. He held multiple professorships at the University of Munich (1893–1916) and led the Museum Fünf Kontinente from 1907.

Luciano Petech worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology, having studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at the University of Allahabad, held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and served as IATS president (c. 1979–1989).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (c. 1876–1879) and the Sorbonne, and he was on the faculty at the University of Paris from circa 1899 to 1927.

Linguist Lucien Tesniere studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig University, and the École des langues orientales, also studying under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the universities of Ljubljana and Strasbourg (1924–1937) and the University of Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and she also studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Indologist and linguist Ludo Rocher studied at Ghent University and SOAS, learning from Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda, among others. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1966) and later Chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studying under Walther Schubring and Heinrich Lüders at Hamburg and Berlin. He taught at the universities of Allahabad, Berlin, and Münster, before holding the chair of Indian history and culture at Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Ewald and held posts at the universities of Greifswald, Jena, Bonn (c. 1862–1872), and Tübingen (c. 1872–1879).

Ludwig Heller specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his Habilitation at Greifswald, where he became an associate professor in 1904, later holding a post at the University of Tartu in 1918.

Ludwig Lange studied at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen, where he studied under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Göttingen, Charles University, the University of Giessen (c. 1859–1871), and Leipzig University (c. 1871–1885).

Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge, where he earned his Ph.D. He taught as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at Cambridge and Trinity College between 1929 and 1947.
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer and worked as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi, and he held a post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1937.

Luis O. Gómez specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler and degrees from Michigan and Puerto Rico. He served as department chair and professor at the University of Michigan and academic director at Mangalam Research Center.
